quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is available.
If no right lane exists, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This lets the tailgater pass you.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, move to the right lane if possible. If no right lane exists, slow down gradually when it is safe to do so. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Get ready to stop because the light will turn red soon.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and look both ways. Check for traffic coming from both directions before crossing.

questions.question: The road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line in the center. The broken line is on your side. When can you pass?

options.text: If the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if no traffic is coming from the other direction.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should they do?

options.text: Drive normally because emotions do not affect driving.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting the car.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting the car.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions distract you from driving. Your mind focuses on the emotion instead of the road. Always take time to calm down and clear your mind before you drive.

questions.question: What does a pennant-shaped sign mean?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign also has text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: When you see an accident ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived yet.

questions.explanation: Only stop if you are involved in the accident or if no emergency help is there. Keep your focus on driving and watch for people near the road. Do not stop just to look at an accident.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass even if it is dangerous.
You can pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, what must other drivers allow for?

options.text: Trucks need more distance to stop.
Trucks need less distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more space to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see the road ahead.

questions.question: What happens when a driver is distracted?

options.text: The driver reacts more slowly to hazards.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver reacts more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down your reaction time to dangers on the road. Distracted driving is always unsafe.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do with your steering wheel?

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn the wheel away from the curb.
Turn the wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill by a curb, set the parking brake and turn the wheel away from the curb. If the car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads with a median between them. You must stay to the right.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop sign intersection:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to indicate that they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You must yield and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.
Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles that use a siren or flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through first before pulling over.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
The condition and type of your vehicle's tires.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road surface, and speed. Time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.
Accelerate to a speed that is faster than the speed of traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
Accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. This helps you blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: When may you honk your horn?

options.text: Have lost control of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: You should honk your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers of the danger.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Drive with your flashers turned on.
Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or siren approaches you on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: May you drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing?

options.text: As long as an approaching train is not too close.
If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
If you first look carefully in both directions.

questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are white with black markings and drivers must always follow them.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What helps a person recover from drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person recover from alcohol. Nothing else will speed up this process.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead is low. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (in this case, 13 feet, 6 inches).

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by driving:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.
